stem.en: A cloudy white liquid shows a bright beam path. After ten minutes nothing has settled. Nothing stays on the filter paper. What can you say about it?

text.en: It is a solution, because it passed through the filter paper just as salt water does.
It is the same kind of mixture as chalk and water, because both scatter the beam.
One of the tests must be wrong, because the three results do not agree with each other.
It is not a solution, because the beam shows particles too small to settle or stay on paper.

explanation.en: A beam path means particles are scattering light, so this is not a solution. The particles are small: they do not settle, and they pass through the paper. That is why option a fails, because passing through paper does not prove a solution. Option b fails because chalk settles and stays on the paper. Option c fails because the tests agree: each one reports something different.

hints.en: A solution shows no beam path at all. What does a bright path tell you?
Filter paper has tiny holes. What can pass through them?
